# ggpyramid

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/matanhakim/ggpyramid/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/matanhakim/ggpyramid/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

ggpyramid is a [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org) extension for building
population pyramids: back-to-back bar charts of a population by age group and
sex. A pyramid is one more layer in an ordinary ggplot, so scales, facets,
themes and further layers work as they do anywhere else in ggplot2. The package
is in early development.

## Installation

You can install the development version of ggpyramid from
[GitHub](https://github.com/matanhakim/ggpyramid) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("matanhakim/ggpyramid")
```

## Example

`geom_pyramid()` draws the bars. It sums a value when one is mapped, as here,
and counts rows when it is not, so it accepts both aggregated data and
individual records. The example data are synthetic.

```{r pyramid, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 150}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpyramid)

ages <- c(paste0(seq(0, 80, 5), "-", seq(4, 84, 5)), "85+")
set.seed(1)
pop <- expand.grid(
  age = factor(ages, ages),
  sex = factor(c("Male", "Female"), c("Male", "Female")),
  region = c("North", "South")
)
pop$n <- round(1000 * exp(-as.integer(pop$age) / 9) * runif(nrow(pop), 0.9, 1.1))

ggplot(subset(pop, region == "North"), aes(x = n, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_pyramid(width = 1, colour = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = abs) +
  labs(x = "Population", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

`denominator` turns the bars into proportions, of the whole panel or of each
side, and each facet gets its own denominator.

```{r proportions, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 150}
ggplot(pop, aes(x = n, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_pyramid(denominator = "side", width = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) scales::percent(abs(x))) +
  facet_wrap(vars(region)) +
  labs(x = "Share of each sex", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

`position_pyramid()` does the mirroring, so any other layer can join the
pyramid with `position = "pyramid"`:

```{r labels, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 150}
ggplot(subset(pop, region == "North"), aes(x = n, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_pyramid(width = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n, hjust = -0.15), position = "pyramid", size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, expand = expansion(mult = 0.1)) +
  labs(x = "Population", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The side of each bar comes from `fill` unless `side` is mapped. Mapping it
separately stacks subgroups within each side:

```{r subgroups, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 150}
ggplot(pop, aes(x = n, y = age, fill = region, side = sex)) +
  geom_pyramid(width = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = abs) +
  labs(x = "Population", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```
